newsitem.title: UK: Abbey may bid 2.2 mln stg for ScotAm - paper.
newsitem.headline: Abbey may bid 2.2 mln stg for ScotAm - paper.

text.p: Britain's Abbey National Plc's increased bid for mutually-owned life assurance group Scottish Amicable could put a headline value of 2.2 billion pounds ($3.61 billion) on the Stirling-based firm, the Sunday Times reported.

The paper said Abbey, which on Friday said it was working towards making a final offer following the entrance of Prudential Corp Plc into the race for ScotAm, would involve a low-interest loan of more than a billion pounds to ScotAm "to boost its key with-profits funds".
Abbey's initial approach was worth more than 1.4 billion pounds, but it was trumped by Prudential's 1.9 billion bid.
Analysts believe other bidders, including overseas insurance firms, may be tempted to make a bid for ScotAm, although none have yet emerged.
They say Prudential is well placed because it can make its offer for ScotAm without having to draw deeply on shareholder funds. ($1=.6097 Pound)
